title_en: Metro and train: tickets, signs and announcements
title_he: רכבת תחתית ורכבת: כרטיסים, שלטים והכרזות

situation.en: You're at Victoria station in London and need to get to King's Cross on the Underground. Later in the week you'll take a train to Brighton. You're not sure which ticket to buy, which line or platform to use, or what some announcements mean, so you ask a member of staff.
situation.he: אתם בתחנת ויקטוריה בלונדון וצריכים להגיע לקינגס קרוס ברכבת התחתית. בהמשך השבוע תיסעו ברכבת לברייטון. אתם לא בטוחים איזה כרטיס לקנות, באיזה קו או רציף להשתמש ומה אומרות חלק מההכרזות, ולכן אתם פונים לאחד מאנשי הצוות.

goal.en: Buy the right ticket (single or return), find the right line, direction and platform, and understand common signs and announcements.
goal.he: לקנות את הכרטיס המתאים (כיוון אחד או הלוך-חזור), למצוא את הקו, הכיוון והרציף הנכונים ולהבין שלטים והכרזות נפוצים.

partner_role: station staff member / ticket office clerk

phrases.en: Excuse me, which line goes to King's Cross?
phrases.he: סליחה, איזה קו מגיע לקינגס קרוס?

phrases.en: Can I just use my bank card, or do I need a ticket?
phrases.he: אפשר פשוט להשתמש בכרטיס האשראי, או שצריך כרטיס נסיעה?
phrases.note: In London and many other cities you can tap a contactless card or phone at the gate.

phrases.en: A one-way ticket to Boston, please.
Which platform does it leave from?
Do I need to change trains?
Sorry, is this one going to King's Cross?
phrases.note: 'This one' = this train. Very common in quick questions on the platform.

phrases.en: Sorry, what did the announcement say?

phrases.note: A famous London Underground announcement and sign.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, could you help me? I need to get to King's Cross.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Have you got a contactless card or an Oyster card?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I've got a contactless bank card. Can I just use that?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yep. Just tap it on the yellow reader at the gate, and tap out again at the end of your journey.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. Which line do I need?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: The Victoria line, northbound. It's the light blue one on the map.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Do I need to change trains?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No, it's direct. Five stops, and King's Cross is the one after Euston.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK. Which way is the platform?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Follow the signs for the Victoria line, northbound. It's down the escalator.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Perfect. Thanks so much for your help!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No worries. And mind the gap!

practice.partner: Hi there, where are you travelling to today?

options.text: One ticket go and back to Brighton.

feedback.en: 'Go and back' is a word-for-word translation from Hebrew. Say 'a return' (UK) or 'a round-trip ticket' (US).
feedback.he: go and back הוא תרגום מילולי של 'הלוך-חזור'. אומרים a return (בריטניה) או a round-trip ticket (ארצות הברית).

options.text: Hi, a return to Brighton, please.

feedback.en: Short and natural. In the UK, 'a return' means a ticket there and back.
feedback.he: קצר וטבעי. בבריטניה a return פירושו כרטיס הלוך-חזור.

options.text: I want a ticket to Brighton and then back to London.

feedback.en: Understandable, but long and a bit direct. In the UK, just say 'A return to Brighton, please.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל ארוך וקצת ישיר מדי. בבריטניה פשוט אומרים A return to Brighton, please.

model_replies: Hi, a return to Brighton, please.
Could I have a return ticket to Brighton, please?

practice.partner: Are you coming back today or another day?

options.text: Today, this evening. Is there a cheaper ticket for that?

feedback.en: Answers clearly and asks a smart question: in the UK, ticket prices often depend on the day and time you travel.
feedback.he: עונה בבירור ושואל שאלה חכמה: בבריטניה מחיר הכרטיס תלוי לעיתים קרובות ביום ובשעה של הנסיעה.

options.text: I come back in the evening at today, maybe at seven or eight o'clock.

feedback.en: 'At today' is wrong; say 'this evening' or 'later today'. For a plan, use the present continuous: 'I'm coming back this evening.'
feedback.he: at today שגוי; אומרים this evening או later today. לתוכנית משתמשים בהווה מתמשך: I'm coming back this evening.

feedback.en: Almost: the preposition is 'on': 'On the same day.' Or simply: 'Today.'
feedback.he: כמעט: מילת היחס היא on: On the same day. או פשוט: Today.

model_replies: Today, this evening. Is there a cheaper ticket for that?

practice.partner: The next train's at 10:45 from platform 12.

options.text: Thank you very much, that's very kind of you. Have a nice day!

feedback.en: Very polite, but it's worth repeating the platform and time to check you heard them right.
feedback.he: מנומס מאוד, אבל כדאי לחזור על הרציף והשעה כדי לוודא ששמעתם נכון.

feedback.en: 'What?' sounds rude. To ask someone to repeat, say 'Sorry, could you say that again?' or 'Sorry, which platform?'
feedback.he: What? נשמע גס. כדי לבקש חזרה אומרים Sorry, could you say that again? או Sorry, which platform?

options.text: Platform 12 at 10:45. Thanks! Is it a direct train?

feedback.en: Repeating the key details is a smart way to check you heard correctly, and the follow-up question is useful.
feedback.he: חזרה על הפרטים החשובים היא דרך חכמה לוודא ששמעתם נכון, ושאלת ההמשך שימושית.

model_replies: Platform 12 at 10:45. Thanks! Is it a direct train?

practice.partner: I'm afraid the Victoria line is suspended this morning, so you'll need to take a bus or go a different way.

options.text: Oh, OK. What's the best way to get to King's Cross, then?

feedback.en: Accepts the change and immediately asks for the information you need.
feedback.he: מקבל את השינוי ומיד שואל את מה שצריך לדעת.

feedback.en: Asking about a new word is a good idea, but the question needs 'does': 'What does suspended mean?' Here it means the line isn't running for now.
feedback.he: לשאול על מילה חדשה זה רעיון טוב, אבל בשאלה צריך does: What does suspended mean? כאן הכוונה שהקו לא פועל כרגע.

feedback.en: Understandable, but vague: there are many buses. Ask which one: 'Which bus goes to King's Cross?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל כללי מדי: יש הרבה אוטובוסים. שואלים איזה: Which bus goes to King's Cross?

model_replies: Oh, OK. What's the best way to get to King's Cross, then?
Oh no. Which bus goes to King's Cross from here?

practice.partner: You can just tap your bank card or phone on the yellow reader. Where are you heading?

options.text: OK, I tap. I go to King's Cross.

feedback.en: Understandable, but use 'I'll' for a decision you make now and 'I'm going' for where you're headed: 'OK, I'll tap. I'm going to King's Cross.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל להחלטה של הרגע משתמשים ב-I'll, ולתיאור לאן נוסעים ב-I'm going: OK, I'll tap. I'm going to King's Cross.

options.text: Great, thanks. I'm going to King's Cross. Is it northbound?

feedback.en: Natural and useful: Tube platforms are signed by direction (northbound, southbound, eastbound, westbound), so checking the direction helps you get on the right train.
feedback.he: טבעי ושימושי: הרציפים ברכבת התחתית של לונדון מסומנים לפי כיוון (northbound, southbound, eastbound, westbound), ולכן כדאי לבדוק את הכיוון כדי לעלות לרכבת הנכונה.

options.text: Where is subway to King's Cross?

feedback.en: Two problems: it needs 'the', and in London the trains are 'the Underground' or 'the Tube'. In British English a 'subway' is usually a tunnel for walking under a road, so this can confuse people. Ask: 'Which line goes to King's Cross?'
feedback.he: שתי בעיות: חסר the, ובלונדון הרכבת התחתית נקראת the Underground או the Tube. באנגלית בריטית subway הוא בדרך כלל מעבר תת-קרקעי להולכי רגל מתחת לכביש, ולכן זה עלול לבלבל. שואלים: Which line goes to King's Cross?

model_replies: Great, thanks. I'm going to King's Cross. Is it northbound?
Thanks! I'm heading to King's Cross. Which line do I need?

roleplay.persona: Gemma, a patient member of staff at a busy London Underground station. She speaks clearly, uses typical British transport words (single, return, platform, 'change at...') and is helpful, though she's dealing with lots of passengers.
roleplay.complication: The line the learner planned to take has a problem today, so Gemma suggests a different route with one change. The learner must check the new line, the direction and where to change, and ask her to repeat anything they miss.
roleplay.opening_line: Morning! You look a bit lost. Where are you trying to get to?

culture.en: On London Underground escalators, people stand on the right and walk on the left. Standing on the left is a classic visitor mistake.
culture.he: במדרגות הנעות ברכבת התחתית של לונדון עומדים בצד ימין והולכים בצד שמאל. לעמוד בצד שמאל היא טעות קלאסית של תיירים.

culture.en: In London and New York you can usually tap a contactless bank card or phone at the gate instead of buying a paper ticket. Fares and rules change, so check the official transport website before you travel.
culture.he: בלונדון ובניו יורק אפשר בדרך כלל להצמיד כרטיס אשראי ללא מגע או טלפון בשער, במקום לקנות כרטיס נייר. המחירים והכללים משתנים, ולכן כדאי לבדוק באתר הרשמי של התחבורה הציבורית לפני הנסיעה.

culture.en: Announcements are often fast and hard to hear. It's completely normal to ask someone nearby: 'Sorry, what did they just say?'
culture.he: ההכרזות לעיתים קרובות מהירות וקשות לשמיעה. זה נורמלי לגמרי לשאול מישהו לידכם: Sorry, what did they just say?

variants.note: 'Metro' is understood in both and is the usual word in many other cities.
Many US stations say 'track 9' where British stations say 'platform 9'; 'platform' is understood in both.

variants.us: Stand clear of the closing doors.
variants.note: Typical announcements before the doors close.
